paper.title_en: Suppression, flow, and chemical components of heavy flavor hadrons in relativistic heavy-ion collisions within an improved Langevin framework
paper.abstract_en: We improve the Langevin model to incorporate both perturbative and non-perturbative interactions between heavy quarks and the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The transport coefficient of heavy quarks is evaluated by a potential scattering model in which both the short-range Yukawa interaction and the long-range string interaction are included. The updated model provides the correct thermal equilibrium limit of the heavy quark system with the medium background, and improves the accuracy in describing the nuclear modification factor and elliptic flow coefficient of $D$ mesons observed at RHIC and the LHC. Nuclear modification of different chemical components of charm hadrons, including $D^0$, $D_s^+$, $Λ_c^+$, $Ξ_c^0$, and $Ω_c^0$, is investigated. Their spectrum ratios are found sensitive to not only the hadronization mechanism of charm quarks but also the medium-modified charm quark spectrum in heavy-ion collisions, offering additional constraints on the heavy quark dynamics inside a color-deconfined nuclear medium.
